get_service_statistics.title: Get service statistics
get_service_statistics.description: Report the service's counters and quotas -- how many indexes, indexers, data sources, skillsets and synonym maps exist, how much storage and vector index size they use, and the maximum each tier allows. Use it to confirm the connection works and to check headroom before creating anything.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: Counters and quotas for each object type on the service.

counters.description: documentCount, indexesCount, indexersCount, dataSourcesCount, storageSize, synonymMaps, skillsetCount, vectorIndexSize -- each with usage and quota.

limits.description: Per-index ceilings for the service tier: fields, complex collections, scoring profiles.

list_indexes.title: List indexes
list_indexes.description: List every index on the service with its full definition -- fields, analyzers, scoring profiles, vector search and semantic configuration. Pass select to fetch just the names when that is all you need.

select.description: Comma-separated top-level properties to return, e.g. "name" for names only.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: Every index definition on the service.

items.description: An index: name, fields, scoringProfiles, vectorSearch, semantic.

get_index.title: Get an index
get_index.description: Read one index's definition: its fields and their attributes (searchable, filterable, facetable, sortable, key, retrievable), analyzers, suggesters, scoring profiles, CORS options and vector/semantic configuration. Read this before create_or_update_index, which replaces the whole object.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The index definition.

fields.description: Each with name, type and its searchable/filterable/facetable/sortable/key flags.

create_index.title: Create an index
create_index.description: Create a new index from a definition. fields is required and every index needs exactly one field with key true, of type Edm.String. Vector fields additionally need dimensions and a vectorSearchProfile that vector_search defines. Fails with 409 if the name is taken -- use create_or_update_index to overwrite.

name.description: Index name -- lower case, digits and dashes, 128 characters or fewer.

fields.description: Field definitions. Each is an object with name and type (Edm.String, Edm.Int32, Edm.Double, Edm.Boolean, Edm.DateTimeOffset, Edm.GeographyPoint, Collection(Edm.Single) for vectors, ...) plus the attribute flags. Exactly one field must have key true.

suggesters.description: Suggester definitions enabling suggest and autocomplete over named fields.

scoring_profiles.description: Scoring profiles that weight fields or apply boosting functions.

analyzers.description: Custom analyzer definitions referenced by the fields.

vector_search.description: Vector search algorithms, profiles and vectorizers used by vector fields.

semantic.description: Semantic ranking configurations, naming the title, content and keyword fields.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The created index definition, as stored.

create_or_update_index.title: Create or replace an index
create_or_update_index.description: Write an index definition at a known name, creating it if absent and replacing it if present. This is a full replace, so send the complete definition -- get_index first and amend it. Adding a new field is allowed on an existing index; changing or removing an existing field is not, and needs a rebuild. Pass allow_index_downtime to add a field that requires the index to go offline briefly.

index_name.description: Name of the index to create or replace.

fields.description: The complete field list. Exactly one field must have key true.

suggesters.description: Suggester definitions enabling suggest and autocomplete over named fields.

scoring_profiles.description: Scoring profiles that weight fields or apply boosting functions.

analyzers.description: Custom analyzer definitions referenced by the fields.

cors_options.description: Cross-origin settings for browser clients calling the index directly.

vector_search.description: Vector search algorithms, profiles and vectorizers used by vector fields.

semantic.description: Semantic ranking configurations, naming the title, content and keyword fields.

similarity.description: Ranking algorithm the index scores with.

allow_index_downtime.description: Allow the index to go offline for seconds so a new field can be added.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The stored index definition after the write.

delete_index.title: Delete an index
delete_index.description: Drop an index and every document in it. The documents are not recoverable and any indexer or alias pointing at the index starts failing, so confirm the name before calling this.

index_name.description: Name of the index to delete.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: Empty on success -- the service answers 204 No Content.

get_index_statistics.title: Get index statistics
get_index_statistics.description: Report how many documents an index holds and how much storage and vector index space it uses. This is the cheapest way to confirm an indexer run actually landed documents.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: Document count and storage used by the index.

analyze_text.title: Test an analyzer on text
analyze_text.description: Show the tokens an analyzer produces for a string, against a real index's configuration. This is how to debug why a query does not match: run the query text and the document text through the same analyzer and compare the tokens. Give either analyzer, or tokenizer with optional filters.

index_name.description: Index whose analyzer configuration to use.

text.description: The text to break into tokens.

analyzer.description: Named analyzer to use, e.g. standard.lucene or en.microsoft. Give this or tokenizer.

tokenizer.description: Tokenizer name, when testing a tokenizer plus filters rather than a whole analyzer.

token_filters.description: Token filters to apply after the tokenizer, e.g. ["lowercase"].

char_filters.description: Character filters to apply before the tokenizer.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The tokens produced, each with its text and offsets.

search_documents.title: Search an index
search_documents.description: Run a query against an index and return matching documents. Covers all four retrieval styles: keyword search via search, structured filtering via filter (OData syntax), vector similarity via vector_queries, and semantic reranking via query_type "semantic" with semantic_configuration. Combine them freely -- a hybrid query is just search plus vector_queries. Leave search as "*" to match everything and filter instead.

search.description: Query text in simple or full Lucene syntax. "*" matches every document.

filter.description: OData filter over filterable fields, e.g. rating ge 4 and category eq 'Luxury'.

top.description: How many documents to return -- the page size.

skip.description: How many matches to skip, for paging. Cannot exceed 100000.

select.description: Comma-separated fields to return. Fetching fewer fields is markedly faster.

orderby.description: Comma-separated sort, e.g. "rating desc, name asc". Omit to sort by relevance.

search_fields.description: Comma-separated searchable fields to match against, instead of all of them.

search_mode.description: Whether any or all of the query terms must match.

query_type.description: simple for the default syntax, full for Lucene syntax (fuzzy, proximity, regex), semantic to rerank the top results with the semantic ranker.

semantic_configuration.description: Name of the index's semantic configuration. Required when query_type is semantic.

vector_queries.description: Vector queries to run. Each is an object with kind ("vector" with a vector array, or "text" to let an index vectorizer embed the string), k, and the fields to search.

vector_filter_mode.description: Whether filter runs before or after the vector search.

facets.description: Facet expressions over facetable fields, e.g. ["category", "rating,interval:1"].

highlight.description: Comma-separated fields to return hit highlights for.

highlight_pre_tag.description: Tag placed before each highlighted fragment.

highlight_post_tag.description: Tag placed after each highlighted fragment.

scoring_profile.description: Name of a scoring profile defined on the index, to weight the ranking.

minimum_coverage.description: Percentage of the index that must be available for the query to succeed.

count.description: Include the total number of matches alongside the page.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The matching documents, with scores and any facets or total count requested.

value.description: Each document, with @search.score and @search.rerankerScore under semantic ranking.

@odata.count.description: Total matches, when count was true.

@search.answers.description: Semantic answers, under semantic query type.

get_document.title: Get one document by key
get_document.description: Look a single document up by its key field. Faster and cheaper than a filtered search when the key is already known; returns 404 when no document has that key.

key.description: Value of the index's key field for the document.

select.description: Comma-separated fields to return instead of the whole document.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The document, with its fields as stored in the index.

count_documents.title: Count documents in an index
count_documents.description: Return how many documents the index currently holds, as a plain number. Use it after indexing to confirm the count moved; note the counter is updated asynchronously and can lag a write by a few seconds.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The document count, as a plain-text integer.

suggest.title: Suggest matching documents as you type
suggest.description: Return document suggestions for a partial query, for a type-ahead box that shows real results. Needs a suggester defined on the index, named in suggester_name. Use autocomplete instead when you want completed query terms rather than documents.

search.description: The partial text typed so far. At least one character.

suggester_name.description: Name of the suggester defined on the index.

filter.description: OData filter narrowing which documents may be suggested.

select.description: Comma-separated fields to return with each suggestion.

search_fields.description: Comma-separated fields to search, which must be covered by the suggester.

orderby.description: Comma-separated sort expression for the suggestions.

fuzzy.description: Tolerate a one-character spelling slip in the typed text.

highlight_pre_tag.description: Tag placed before the matched fragment of each suggestion.

highlight_post_tag.description: Tag placed after the matched fragment of each suggestion.

minimum_coverage.description: Percentage of the index that must be available for the request to succeed.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The suggested documents, each with the matched text.

autocomplete.title: Autocomplete a query term
autocomplete.description: Complete the term being typed, using the terms actually present in the index. Returns query text, not documents -- reach for suggest when the type-ahead should show matching records instead. Needs a suggester on the index.

search.description: The partial term typed so far.

suggester_name.description: Name of the suggester defined on the index.

autocomplete_mode.description: oneTerm completes the last term; twoTerms completes it and predicts the next; oneTermWithContext completes the last term using the terms before it.

filter.description: OData filter narrowing which documents contribute terms.

search_fields.description: Comma-separated fields to draw terms from, covered by the suggester.

fuzzy.description: Tolerate a one-character spelling slip in the typed text.

highlight_pre_tag.description: Tag placed before the completed portion of each term.

highlight_post_tag.description: Tag placed after the completed portion of each term.

minimum_coverage.description: Percentage of the index that must be available for the request to succeed.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The completed terms, with the query text each would produce.

index_documents.title: Upload, merge or delete documents
index_documents.description: Push a batch of document actions into an index. Each action carries "@search.action" -- upload (insert or replace), merge (update an existing document, failing if absent), mergeOrUpload, or delete -- alongside the document's fields; delete needs only the key field. Up to 1000 actions or 16 MB per call. The response reports success per document, and a 207 means some actions failed while others succeeded, so check every entry.

actions.description: The document actions. Each is the document's fields plus an "@search.action" of upload, merge, mergeOrUpload or delete.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: One result per action, in the order sent.

list_indexers.title: List indexers
list_indexers.description: List every indexer on the service with its definition -- which data source it reads, which index it writes, its schedule, field mappings and any skillset it runs.

select.description: Comma-separated top-level properties to return, e.g. "name".

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: Every indexer definition on the service.

items.description: name, dataSourceName, targetIndexName, skillsetName, schedule, parameters.

get_indexer.title: Get an indexer
get_indexer.description: Read one indexer's definition, including its schedule, batch and error thresholds, field mappings and output field mappings. Use get_indexer_status instead to see whether it is running or failing.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The indexer definition.

create_indexer.title: Create an indexer
create_indexer.description: Create an indexer that reads a data source and writes into an index, on a schedule or on demand. The data source and target index must already exist. Creating an indexer runs it once immediately unless disabled is true.

data_source_name.description: Name of an existing data source connection to read from.

target_index_name.description: Name of the existing index to write documents into.

skillset_name.description: Skillset to run over each document during indexing, for AI enrichment.

description.description: Free-text note describing what this indexer is for.

schedule.description: Run schedule, e.g. {"interval": "PT1H"} for hourly. Omit to run on demand only.

parameters.description: Batch size, failure thresholds and parsing configuration for the run.

field_mappings.description: Mappings from source fields to index fields, with optional mapping functions.

output_field_mappings.description: Mappings from skillset outputs to index fields.

disabled.description: Create the indexer without running or scheduling it.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The created indexer definition.

create_or_update_indexer.title: Create or replace an indexer
create_or_update_indexer.description: Write an indexer definition at a known name, creating it if absent and replacing it if present. A full replace -- get_indexer first and amend the object, or fields you leave out are cleared. Updating an indexer resets its change-tracking state and re-runs it from the beginning.

indexer_name.description: Name of the indexer to create or replace.

data_source_name.description: Name of an existing data source connection to read from.

target_index_name.description: Name of the existing index to write documents into.

skillset_name.description: Skillset to run over each document during indexing, for AI enrichment.

description.description: Free-text note describing what this indexer is for.

parameters.description: Batch size, failure thresholds and parsing configuration for the run.

field_mappings.description: Mappings from source fields to index fields, with optional mapping functions.

output_field_mappings.description: Mappings from skillset outputs to index fields.

disabled.description: Leave the indexer in place but stop it running or scheduling.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The stored indexer definition after the write.

delete_indexer.title: Delete an indexer
delete_indexer.description: Remove an indexer. The index it wrote and the data source it read are left alone -- only the indexer and its execution history go.

indexer_name.description: Name of the indexer to delete.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: Empty on success -- the service answers 204 No Content.

run_indexer.title: Run an indexer now
run_indexer.description: Start an indexer run immediately, outside its schedule. Returns as soon as the run is accepted (202), so poll get_indexer_status to see whether it succeeded. Calling this while a run is in progress returns 409.

indexer_name.description: Name of the indexer to run.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: Empty on success -- the run was accepted and is now in progress.

reset_indexer.title: Reset an indexer's change tracking
reset_indexer.description: Clear the indexer's high-water mark so its next run reprocesses every document from the start rather than only what changed. Pair with run_indexer to force a full re-index; use reset_documents instead to redo only specific documents.

indexer_name.description: Name of the indexer to reset.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: Empty on success -- the service answers 204 No Content.

reset_documents.title: Reset specific documents for reprocessing
reset_documents.description: Mark named documents so the indexer's next run reprocesses just those, rather than resetting the whole indexer. Identify them by index key or by data source document id. Pass overwrite to replace the pending reset list instead of adding to it.

indexer_name.description: Name of the indexer whose documents to reset.

document_keys.description: Key values of the documents in the target index. Give this or datasource_document_ids.

datasource_document_ids.description: Document identifiers as they appear in the data source.

overwrite.description: Replace the existing list of documents pending reset rather than appending.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: Empty on success -- the service answers 204 No Content.

get_indexer_status.title: Get an indexer's status and history
get_indexer_status.description: Report whether an indexer is running, idle or in error, plus the result of the last run and a history of recent ones with item counts and the first errors and warnings. This is the tool to reach for when documents are not appearing in an index.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: Current state, the last run's outcome, and recent execution history.

lastResult.description: status, itemsProcessed, itemsFailed, errorMessage, startTime, endTime.

list_data_sources.title: List data source connections
list_data_sources.description: List every data source connection defined on the service -- the Azure Blob, Azure SQL, Cosmos DB, Table Storage or ADLS Gen2 sources indexers read from. Credentials in the connection strings come back redacted.

select.description: Comma-separated top-level properties to return, e.g. "name".

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: Every data source definition on the service.

get_data_source.title: Get a data source connection
get_data_source.description: Read one data source's definition: its type, container or table, change and deletion detection policies. The connection string is returned redacted, so this cannot be used to recover a credential.

data_source_name.description: Name of the data source connection.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The data source definition, with credentials redacted.

create_data_source.title: Create a data source connection
create_data_source.description: Define where an indexer reads from. type is the source kind (azureblob, azuresql, cosmosdb, azuretable, adlsgen2), credentials holds the connection string, and container names the blob container, table or collection. Add a change detection policy so later runs pick up only what changed.

type.description: Kind of source the indexer will read.

credentials.description: Connection details, as {"connectionString": "..."} -- or a managed identity connection string.

container.description: What to read: {"name": "<container-or-table>", "query": "<optional folder or query>"}.

data_change_detection_policy.description: How the indexer spots changed rows, e.g. a high water mark column policy.

data_deletion_detection_policy.description: How the indexer spots deleted rows, e.g. a soft delete column policy.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The created data source definition, with credentials redacted.

create_or_update_data_source.title: Create or replace a data source connection
create_or_update_data_source.description: Write a data source definition at a known name, creating it if absent and replacing it if present. A full replace, so send every field you want kept -- including credentials, which cannot be read back and must be supplied again.

data_source_name.description: Name of the data source to create or replace.

type.description: Kind of source the indexer will read.

credentials.description: Connection details, as {"connectionString": "..."}. Must be resent on every update.

container.description: What to read: {"name": "<container-or-table>", "query": "<optional folder or query>"}.

data_change_detection_policy.description: How the indexer spots changed rows.

data_deletion_detection_policy.description: How the indexer spots deleted rows.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The stored data source definition after the write.

delete_data_source.title: Delete a data source connection
delete_data_source.description: Remove a data source definition. Any indexer still pointing at it will fail on its next run, so repoint or delete those first.

data_source_name.description: Name of the data source to delete.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: Empty on success -- the service answers 204 No Content.

list_skillsets.title: List skillsets
list_skillsets.description: List every skillset on the service. A skillset is the AI enrichment pipeline an indexer runs over each document -- OCR, entity recognition, chunking, embedding generation and custom web API skills.

select.description: Comma-separated top-level properties to return, e.g. "name".

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: Every skillset definition on the service.

get_skillset.title: Get a skillset
get_skillset.description: Read one skillset's definition: the ordered skills, their inputs and outputs, the Azure AI Services key it bills enrichment to, and any knowledge store or index projections it writes.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The skillset definition.

create_or_update_skillset.title: Create or replace a skillset
create_or_update_skillset.description: Write a skillset at a known name, creating it if absent and replacing it if present. skills is an ordered list where each entry names its "@odata.type" (OcrSkill, SplitSkill, AzureOpenAIEmbeddingSkill, WebApiSkill, ...), its context, and how its inputs map to earlier outputs. Anything beyond the free enrichment tier needs cognitive_services to bill against.

skillset_name.description: Name of the skillset to create or replace.

skills.description: The ordered skills. Each has an "@odata.type", a context path such as "/document", and inputs and outputs wiring it to the enrichment tree.

description.description: Free-text note describing what the skillset enriches.

cognitive_services.description: Azure AI Services resource key that billable skills are charged to.

knowledge_store.description: Where to project enriched output as tables, objects or files in Azure Storage.

index_projections.description: How to project enriched chunks into one or more search indexes.

encryption_key.description: Customer-managed key in Azure Key Vault to encrypt the definition with.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The stored skillset definition after the write.

delete_skillset.title: Delete a skillset
delete_skillset.description: Remove a skillset. Any indexer that references it will fail on its next run until it is repointed or the reference is dropped.

skillset_name.description: Name of the skillset to delete.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: Empty on success -- the service answers 204 No Content.

list_synonym_maps.title: List synonym maps
list_synonym_maps.description: List every synonym map on the service. A synonym map expands query terms at search time, so "wifi" also matches "wireless internet" without re-indexing anything.

select.description: Comma-separated top-level properties to return, e.g. "name".

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: Every synonym map on the service.

items.description: name, format and the synonyms rules.

get_synonym_map.title: Get a synonym map
get_synonym_map.description: Read one synonym map's rules. The rules are newline-separated Solr syntax: "usa, united states" for equivalence, "washington, wash => wa" for explicit mapping.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The synonym map, with its rules.

create_or_update_synonym_map.title: Create or replace a synonym map
create_or_update_synonym_map.description: Write a synonym map at a known name, creating it if absent and replacing it if present. synonyms is one rule per line in Solr syntax. The map only takes effect once a field on the index names it in synonymMaps, which is an index update.

synonym_map_name.description: Name of the synonym map to create or replace.

synonyms.description: The rules, one per line, in Solr syntax -- "usa, united states" for equivalent terms, "wash => washington" for explicit mapping.
synonyms.example:
usa, united states, united states of america
wash => washington

encryption_key.description: Customer-managed key in Azure Key Vault to encrypt the map with.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The stored synonym map after the write.

delete_synonym_map.title: Delete a synonym map
delete_synonym_map.description: Remove a synonym map. Delete it only once no index field references it -- the service rejects the call while a field still names the map.

synonym_map_name.description: Name of the synonym map to delete.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: Empty on success -- the service answers 204 No Content.

list_aliases.title: List index aliases
list_aliases.description: List every alias on the service. An alias is a stable name that points at one index, so applications can query "products" while you rebuild behind it and repoint the alias at the new index.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: Every alias, with the index each points at.

get_alias.title: Get an index alias
get_alias.description: Read one alias and the index it currently resolves to. Useful for confirming which index is live before or after a rebuild swap.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The alias and the index it points at.

create_alias.title: Create an index alias
create_alias.description: Create a stable query name pointing at one index. indexes takes exactly one index name -- an alias maps to a single index at a time. Fails with 409 when the name is already an alias or an index.

name.description: The alias name applications will query.

indexes.description: Exactly one index name for the alias to resolve to.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The created alias.

create_or_update_alias.title: Create or repoint an index alias
create_or_update_alias.description: Point an alias at an index, creating the alias if it does not exist. This is the swap step of a zero-downtime rebuild: build the new index, then repoint the alias. Allow up to ten seconds for the change to reach every query replica.

alias_name.description: Name of the alias to create or repoint.

indexes.description: Exactly one index name for the alias to resolve to.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: The alias after the write.

delete_alias.title: Delete an index alias
delete_alias.description: Remove an alias. The index it pointed at is untouched, but any client querying through the alias starts getting 404s immediately.

alias_name.description: Name of the alias to delete.

api_version.description: Search REST API version to call.

output.description: Empty on success -- the service answers 204 No Content.
